profile.campus: Secaucus / North Bergen, Hudson County, New Jersey (Equinix New York metro campus)
profile.reading:
Per Equinix own site, this NY4 facility is located at 755 Secaucus Rd, Secaucus, NJ 07094 and totals 151,771 sq ft. Redundancy: N+1 Power redundancy, N+1 Cooling redundancy; minimum cabinet density 5kVA, 120v/208v power distribution. No MW power capacity figure is published on this page.

Equinix's wider New York/New Jersey metro, anchored by this Secaucus-area campus, comprised nine data centers totaling roughly 739,000 square feet of technical space as of a 2026 Data Center Frontier report, which also detailed the neighboring NY5 building's history: built in 2012 and expanded in 2016 to 20 megawatts of critical power capacity, with four utility feeder lines and eight 2.5-megawatt backup generators, and the campus remained operational for a full week without grid power during Superstorm Sandy in 2012. The campus houses matching engines for major stock-exchange electronic trading and serves financial-services firms seeking proximity to Wall Street with far more colocation space than Manhattan itself can offer; nearby NY11 in Carteret, NJ primarily serves Nasdaq and was being expanded to host an AWS Local Zone as of the same report.

Equinix, the operator, was founded in 1998 by Al Avery and Jay Adelson and has grown into a global colocation and interconnection provider operating more than 260 data centers across over 70 metros worldwide; the company converted to a real estate investment trust (REIT) in 2015. Within its International Business Exchange (IBX) portfolio, buildings like this one offer private cages and suites, Equinix Fabric software-defined interconnection, Internet Exchange peering, and cross-connects linking enterprises directly to cloud on-ramps for AWS, Microsoft Azure, Google Cloud, Oracle Cloud, and IBM Cloud.

This Secaucus/North Bergen cluster sits in Hudson County, New Jersey, roughly 10 miles from Lower Manhattan; the area's lower real estate costs and proximity to the Wall Street financial corridor, rather than any single anchor tenant, are what have concentrated Equinix's largest East Coast metro campus here rather than in New York City itself.

reading.body:
Equinix NY4 is a 151,771 square-foot facility in Secaucus, New Jersey, part of the nine-building Equinix New York metro campus spanning roughly 739,000 square feet across Hudson County. The operator publishes no megawatt capacity figure for NY4 itself, though a neighboring NY5 building in the same campus was expanded to 20 megawatts of critical power capacity. The facility offers N+1 power and cooling redundancy with a minimum cabinet density of 5 kilowatts per cabinet, standard for colocation infrastructure.

The Secaucus campus sits 10 miles from Lower Manhattan and concentrates Equinix's largest East Coast presence because of lower real estate costs and proximity to Wall Street rather than a single anchor tenant. The campus has historically served major financial services firms seeking colocation space closer to the trading floor than Manhattan itself provides, and remained operational for a full week without grid power during Superstorm Sandy in 2012. The wider metro region hosts matching engines for major stock-exchange electronic trading and cloud on-ramps for AWS, Microsoft Azure, Google Cloud, Oracle Cloud, and IBM Cloud.

New Jersey has 48 mapped data center facilities, of which only 5 have published megawatt capacity, totaling 111.3 megawatts. This campus does not publish its MW figure and therefore does not appear in the state's ranked capacity count. Across the United States, no single megawatt constraint binds Equinix's ability to scale AI infrastructure here, but instead the lack of published power transparency at this facility limits visibility into whether NY4 itself could absorb additional critical load.
